paragraphs.en: Just how much does the Constitution protect your digital data? The Supreme Court will now consider whether police can search the contents of a mobile phone without a warrant if the phone is on or around a person during an arrest.
paragraphs.zh: 宪法究竟在多大程度上保护你的数字数据？最高法院现在将审议这样一个问题：如果警方逮捕一个人时，手机就在此人身上或身旁，警方是否可以在没有搜查令的情况下搜查手机内容。

paragraphs.en: California has asked the justices to refrain from a sweeping ruling, particularly one that upsets the old assumption that authorities may search through the possessions of suspects at the time of their arrest. It is hard, the state argues, for judges to assess the implications of new and rapidly changing technologies.
paragraphs.zh: 加利福尼亚州已要求大法官们避免作出影响广泛的裁决，尤其不要推翻长期以来的一个假定：当局可以在逮捕嫌疑人时搜查其随身物品。该州辩称，法官很难评估日新月异的新技术所带来的影响。

paragraphs.en: The court would be recklessly modest if it followed California’s advice. Enough of the implications are discernable, even obvious, so that the justices can and should provide updated guidelines to police, lawyers and defendants.
paragraphs.zh: 如果法院听从加州的建议，这种谦抑就未免过于轻率。这些影响中，已经有足够多的内容可以辨识，甚至显而易见，因此大法官们能够、也应该为警察、律师和被告提供与时俱进的指导原则。

paragraphs.en: They should start by discarding California’s lame argument that exploring the contents of a smartphone – a vast storehouse of digital information – is similar to, say, going through a suspect’s purse. The court has ruled that police don’t violate the Fourth Amendment when they go through the wallet or pocketbook of an arrestee without a warrant. But exploring one’s smartphone is more like entering his or her home. A smartphone may contain an arrestee’s reading history, financial history, medical history and comprehensive records of recent correspondence. The development of “cloud computing”, meanwhile, has made that exploration so much the easier.
paragraphs.zh: 他们首先应当摒弃加州站不住脚的论点，即查看智能手机这一庞大数字信息库的内容，就像翻查嫌疑人的钱包一样。法院曾裁定，警方在没有搜查令的情况下翻查被捕者的钱包或手提包，并不违反宪法第四修正案。但是，查看一个人的智能手机，更像是进入其住宅。智能手机可能存有被捕者的阅读记录、财务记录、医疗记录，以及近期通信的完整记录。与此同时，“云计算”的发展又使这种探查变得更加容易。

paragraphs.en: Americans should take steps to protect their digital privacy. But keeping sensitive information on these devices is increasingly a requirement of normal life. Citizens still have a right to expect private documents to remain private and protected by the Constitution’s prohibition on unreasonable searches.
paragraphs.zh: 美国人应采取措施保护自己的数字隐私。但是，将敏感信息保存在这些设备上，正日益成为正常生活的必要条件。公民仍然有权期待私人文件保持私密，并受到宪法中禁止不合理搜查条款的保护。

paragraphs.en: As so often is the case, stating that principle doesn’t ease the challenge of line-drawing. In many cases, it would not be overly burdensome for authorities to obtain a warrant to search through phone contents. They could still invalidate Fourth Amendment protections when facing severe, urgent circumstances, and they could take reasonable measures to ensure that phone data are not erased or altered while waiting for a warrant. The court, though, may want to allow room for police to cite situations where they are entitled to more freedom.
paragraphs.zh: 正如许多情况下所见，阐明这一原则并不能减轻划定界限的困难。在许多情况下，当局为搜查手机内容而取得搜查令，并不会构成过重负担。在面临严重、紧迫的情形时，他们仍可不受第四修正案保护条款的限制；在等待搜查令期间，也可以采取合理措施，确保手机数据不被删除或更改。不过，法院可能希望留下一定余地，让警方能够列举有权享有更大行动自由的情形。

paragraphs.en: But the justices should not swallow California’s argument whole. New, disruptive technology sometimes demands novel applications of the Constitution’s protections. Orin Kerr, a law professor, compares the explosion and accessibility of digital information in the 21st century with the establishment of automobile use as a virtual necessity of life in the 20th: The justices had to specify novel rules for the new personal domain of the passenger car then; they must sort out how the Fourth Amendment applies to digital information now.
paragraphs.zh: 但大法官们不应全盘接受加州的论点。具有颠覆性的新技术，有时要求以新方式适用宪法的保护条款。法学教授奥林·克尔将二十一世纪数字信息的爆炸式增长及其获取的便利性，比作二十世纪汽车的使用几乎成为生活必需的过程：当年，大法官们必须为小汽车这一新出现的私人领域制定新规则；如今，他们必须厘清第四修正案如何适用于数字信息。
